audit_status.source_base: Greek Galatians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for heirs/guardians, elemental powers, Abba Spirit, Paul's concern, Hagar/Sarah allegory, freedom-child imagery. Anti-Jewish misuse warning included.

verses.restored: But I say, for as long a time as the heir is an infant, one differs nothing from an enslaved one, though being lord of all,

familiar.text: Now I say, That the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all;

verses.restored: but is under guardians and household managers until the time appointed by the father.

familiar.text: But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father.

verses.restored: So also we, when we were infants, were enslaved under the elemental powers/principles of the world.

familiar.text: Even so we, when we were children, were in bondage under the elements of the world:

verses.restored: But when the fullness of time came, the Divine sent out his Son, come from woman, come under Law,

familiar.text: But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,

verses.restored: so that he might redeem/release those under Law, so that we might receive adoption/placing-as-children.

familiar.text: To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.

verses.restored: And because you are sons/children, the Divine sent out the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, Abba, Father.

familiar.text: And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father.

verses.restored: So you are no longer enslaved but son/child; and if son/child, also heir through the Divine.

familiar.text: Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.

verses.restored: But then, not knowing the Divine, you were enslaved to those by nature not gods.

familiar.text: Howbeit then, when ye knew not God, ye did service unto them which by nature are no gods.

verses.restored: But now, having known the Divine, or rather having been known by the Divine, how do you turn again to the weak and poor elemental powers/principles, to which you want to be enslaved again anew?

familiar.text: But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage?

verses.restored: You observe days and months and seasons and years.

familiar.text: Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years.

verses.restored: I fear for you, lest somehow I have labored into you in vain.

familiar.text: I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain.

verses.restored: Become as I am, because I also became as you, siblings, I beg you. You wronged me in nothing.

familiar.text: Brethren, I beseech you, be as I am; for I am as ye are: ye have not injured me at all.

verses.restored: But you know that through weakness of the flesh I announced good news to you formerly,

familiar.text: Ye know how through infirmity of the flesh I preached the gospel unto you at the first.

verses.restored: and your testing in my flesh you did not despise nor spit out, but received me as a messenger of the Divine, as Messiah Jesus.

familiar.text: And my temptation which was in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.

verses.restored: Where then is your blessedness/flourishing? For I testify to you that, if possible, having dug out your eyes, you would have given them to me.

familiar.text: Where is then the blessedness ye spake of? for I bear you record, that, if it had been possible, ye would have plucked out your own eyes, and have given them to me.

verses.restored: So then have I become your enemy by speaking truth to you?

familiar.text: Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?

verses.restored: They are zealous for you, not beautifully/well, but they want to shut you out, so that you may be zealous for them.

familiar.text: They zealously affect you, but not well; yea, they would exclude you, that ye might affect them.

verses.restored: But it is beautiful/good to be zealous in a beautiful/good thing always, and not only when I am present with you.

familiar.text: But it is good to be zealously affected always in a good thing, and not only when I am present with you.

verses.restored: My children, for whom I again labor in birth until Messiah is formed in you,

familiar.text: My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you,

verses.restored: I wished to be present with you now and to change my voice, because I am perplexed about you.

familiar.text: I desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice; for I stand in doubt of you.

verses.restored: Tell me, you who wish to be under Law, do you not hear the Law?

familiar.text: Tell me, ye that desire to be under the law, do ye not hear the law?

verses.restored: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one from the enslaved woman and one from the free woman.

familiar.text: For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman.

verses.restored: But the one from the enslaved woman was born according to flesh, and the one from the free woman through promise.

familiar.text: But he who was of the bondwoman was born after the flesh; but he of the freewoman was by promise.

verses.restored: These things are being spoken allegorically; for these women are two covenants: one indeed from Mount Sinai bearing children into slavery, which is Hagar.

familiar.text: Which things are an allegory: for these are the two covenants; the one from the mount Sinai, which gendereth to bondage, which is Agar.

verses.restored: Now Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia and corresponds to the present Jerusalem, for she is enslaved with her children.

familiar.text: For this Agar is mount Sinai in Arabia, and answereth to Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children.

verses.restored: But the Jerusalem above is free, who is our mother.

familiar.text: But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all.

verses.restored: For it is written: Rejoice, barren one who does not bear; break forth and cry aloud, you who do not labor in birth, because many are the children of the deserted one, more than of the one having the husband.

familiar.text: For it is written, Rejoice, thou barren that bearest not; break forth and cry, thou that travailest not: for the desolate hath many more children than she which hath an husband.

verses.restored: But you, siblings, according to Isaac, are children of promise.

familiar.text: Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are the children of promise.

verses.restored: But just as then the one born according to flesh pursued/persecuted the one according to Spirit, so also now.

familiar.text: But as then he that was born after the flesh persecuted him that was born after the Spirit, even so it is now.

verses.restored: But what does the Scripture say? Cast out the enslaved woman and her son, for the son of the enslaved woman will certainly not inherit with the son of the free woman.

familiar.text: Nevertheless what saith the scripture? Cast out the bondwoman and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the freewoman.

verses.restored: Therefore, siblings, we are not children of an enslaved woman but of the free woman.

familiar.text: So then, brethren, we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free.

safety_note: Galatians 4's Hagar/Sarah allegory is Paul's sharp argument about covenantal freedom and Gentile inclusion; it must not be turned into contempt for Jewish people, Torah, Jerusalem, or enslaved women. The allegory is rhetorically volatile and should be handled with care.
